| Scene description | • The site lies beside an internal passage in Luguang Community, Hongshan District.<br>• S06-B-01: two boxes accumulate beside a green cabinet and masonry base on gray paving. A large brown YunYan box is damaged with exposed red tape; a green-white YONGTONGFAR box is stained and partly damaged. Paper, debris, gravel, and leaves surround them; no sorting bins are visible. |
| Regulatory basis | • Residential waste management should implement source reduction, sorting, collection, and related duties within the Guidelines' nine settings. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 1.2, [D-16-C001](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Four-category provision should include food/other-waste bins near building entrances and hazardous-waste/recyclables containers in main public passages. No visible sorting bins at this site breach provision standards. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 4.5.4, [D-16-C004](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering, or stockpiling incurs up to CNY 200 for individuals or CNY 5,000–50,000 for organizations. The boxes are interpreted as casual stockpiling meeting these conditions. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 42, [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Failure to sort at designated locations requires correction; individuals refusing correction incur CNY 100–1,000. External disposal is interpreted as non-compliant. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (3), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Penalties for commercial collectors failing duties do not directly apply to this residential conduct but may inform management accountability. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 45, [D-03-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Two accumulations beside a passage create visual pollution and sanitation risks, without overflow or severe environmental or safety impacts. Missing sorting containers indicate management gaps. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: damaged boxes and paper at a public passage edge create visual disorder. Possible short-term impacts: insects, bacteria, combustible-cardboard fire risks, impaired movement experience, and complaints or escalation may follow. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** improper residential disposal of bulky or recyclable materials; damaged taped boxes and absent containers suggest designated points were not used.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** missing or poorly located bins, inconsistent with Section 4.5.4 of the Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** unmet inspection and cleaning duties; verify property/community jurisdiction and routine work.<br>- **Possible cause 4:** unremoved temporary storage; check designated storage status and recent renovation or moving activity. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, sanitation, sorting awareness, and management credibility may decline, penalties under Article 42 of the Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste may follow, and subsequent removal costs may rise. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** remove boxes and scattered materials at S06-B-01, sweep nearby ground, and add temporary no-stockpiling warnings.<br>- **Long-term measures:** (1) provide all four categories at passages and entrances under Section 4.5.4 of the Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings; (2) educate via noticeboards and WeChat; (3) require daily property/community inspections and prompt action; (4) advise or lawfully penalize repeated violations under Article 18(3) of Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification. |
| Priority | **Medium.** Management omissions and improper residential disposal affect a public passage, community image, and residents without severe pollution or safety harm. Short-term rectification should prevent escalation or habitual violations. |
